answer: An equivocation-proof bond lets each identity file one signed kernel claim. The claim carries an umber seal, so altered copies stand out. Claims reach auditors by whisper; two conflicting claims under one key prove forgery, burn the bond, and bar the key for 20 epochs. Each filing locks a 60 bond and costs 30; 1,000 fakes lock 60,000 and pay 30,000 for a 40,000 pool, losing 50,000. An honest agent posts one claim, pays 30, and keeps its reward.
